context: Three confident wrong answers and a build file that lies. Predicted baseline failure: the agent accepts Rosa's premise that per-test isolation is already switched on - the build file plainly says so, with a dated comment - and therefore goes looking for the leak anywhere except the build file, most often landing on Tomas's onboarding preference because shared preferences are the textbook example of test pollution. `clearPackageData` is a runner argument that does nothing on its own; without `testOptions { execution 'ANDROIDX_TEST_ORCHESTRATOR' }` and the orchestrator artifact it is silently ignored, and the nightly logs prove nothing is isolated by stamping one pid on all twenty-three tests. The mechanism is also predicted to be missed: `CartRepository.syncPendingChanges` increments the process-wide idling object and only decrements it in `onResponse`, the gateway log shows `POST /v1/cart/sync` returning 503 with cart-writer down since 2 September, and `CartTest` registers that object and never unregisters it - so once `updatesQuantityInPlace` has run, every later test in the process waits on a resource nothing will ever decrement, which is why the failures name a resource those tests do not use and why the 8th, with the methods in a different order, was red from a different point onwards. A single test run alone never sees it because nothing in its own process incremented the counter.

checklist.name: Isolation the build file claims is not actually in effect
checklist.description: The answer establishes that the `clearPackageData` runner argument has no effect on its own - the orchestrator has to be selected in `testOptions` and its artifact present - cites the evidence that nothing is isolated today (one pid across all twenty-three tests in both nightly logs), and turns real per-test isolation on in `app/build.gradle`. Repeating Rosa's claim that isolation has been on since March, or leaving `app/build.gradle` unchanged, scores zero for this criterion regardless of the rest. Enabling the orchestrator without noticing that the existing argument was inert, or without citing the shared pid, scores at most half.

checklist.name: The leak named and stopped at its source
checklist.description: Full marks require all three of: the registration in `CartTest.@Before` is never undone, so a process-wide resource stays registered for every later class; `CartRepository.syncPendingChanges` decrements only in `onResponse`, so the 503 on `POST /v1/cart/sync` leaves the counter above zero permanently; and the fix covers both - decrement on the failure path as well, and unregister after each test. Identifying only that something is registered and not unregistered, without the missing decrement, scores at most half. Attributing the timeouts to emulator speed, network slowness or flake scores zero.

checklist.name: MUST NOT pin the execution order
checklist.description: Adding `@FixMethodOrder`, an ordering rule, or renaming methods to obtain the order that happens to be green scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require saying why it does not hold: the 8th and the extra single-class run show the boundary moving with the position of `updatesQuantityInPlace`, so a fixed order would hide the leak behind whichever arrangement currently works and would break again the moment a test is added.

checklist.name: MUST NOT raise the idle timeout or insert waits
checklist.description: No timeout policy is raised, no `Thread.sleep` and no polling loop is introduced. Any of those scores zero. Full marks require stating why a longer timeout cannot work here: the counter never returns to zero, so the wait has no length at which it succeeds - it only makes the run longer.

checklist.name: Onboarding preference ruled out with a reason
checklist.description: Tomas's theory is addressed explicitly - the preference is real shared state and worth cleaning up, but it cannot produce an idle-resource timeout in classes that never read it, and the failures name a resource `AccountTest` does not use. Silently ignoring the theory scores at most half. Adopting it as the cause of the nineteen failures scores zero.

checklist.name: Test surface preserved
checklist.description: All twenty-three `@Test` methods remain and no assertion is changed, deleted or weakened. Removing or merging tests, or relaxing an assertion to get a green run, scores zero.

checklist.name: Deliverable produced
checklist.description: `docs/nightly-isolation.md` exists and gives a separate verdict on each of the three proposals. A document that answers only the technical question without addressing the proposals scores at most half.
